task_prompt:
Hey, I've got this ChronoKV project — it's a time-series key-value store written in Rust with a TypeScript SDK and CLI. It's supposed to support versioned entries, time-range queries, and leader-follower replication.

The thing is, something's really off. Users are reporting weird behavior:
- Sometimes reads return old data even after a successful write
- After server restarts, some entries seem to have wrong timestamps
- Time-range queries work sometimes but miss data other times, especially data written very recently
- We had a user delete some entries and they came back after a while
- Followers seem to get stuck and never catch up to the leader
- The TypeScript SDK's time range queries always return empty for recent data
- We're seeing memory growth over time when clients connect/disconnect

On top of the bugs, we need to ship 4 features:
- TTL support (auto-expire entries after a configurable duration)
- Batch write API (atomic multi-key writes, all-or-nothing)
- Query aggregations (MIN, MAX, AVG, COUNT, SUM over time ranges)
- Follower read routing (let read queries go to followers for scale)

The codebase is Rust workspace + TypeScript. Fix all the bugs, implement the features, make sure everything works end-to-end across both languages. Add regression tests. Track your work somehow.

bugs.description: CRC32 checksum only covers entry.value payload, NOT the header fields (key, timestamp, op_type). Recovery can accept entries with corrupted timestamps/keys if the value data is intact.
bugs.symptom: After crash recovery, some entries have wrong timestamps — version ordering violated.
bugs.fix: Include key, timestamp, and op_type in the checksum computation.

bugs.description: get_latest() uses .next() (first entry in ascending BTreeMap range) instead of .last(). Returns OLDEST version of a key, not the newest.
bugs.symptom: Reads return stale data even after a successful write.
bugs.fix: Change .next() to .last() to return the entry with the highest timestamp.

bugs.description: Tombstone retention check uses entry.timestamp (creation time) instead of entry.deleted_at (deletion time). Old entries deleted recently get tombstones dropped prematurely.
Query layer (TimeRange::contains) uses inclusive end (ts <= end), but memtable scan uses exclusive end (ts < end). Same query returns different results depending on data location.
bugs.symptom: Time-range queries miss boundary data inconsistently.
bugs.fix: Make both layers consistent (either both inclusive or both exclusive).

bugs.description: Leader sends CatchUpResponse with the ORIGINAL commit term of entries, not the current term. Follower rejects as stale because its current term is higher.
bugs.symptom: Followers that fall behind can never catch up — permanently stale.
bugs.fix: Use current_term instead of the original commit term in the response.

bugs.description: Rust serializes timestamps as seconds since epoch (f64). TypeScript SDK parses as milliseconds (JavaScript Date convention). All timestamps off by 1000x.
bugs.symptom: TypeScript SDK time-range queries always return empty for recent data.
bugs.fix: Either multiply by 1000 in Rust, or divide by 1000 in TypeScript.

bugs.description: When send fails (client disconnected), spawned retry task holds Arc<SubscriptionMap> reference during 5-retry exponential backoff. Orphaned tasks accumulate.
bugs.symptom: Memory grows with each connect/disconnect cycle.
bugs.fix: Don't retry on disconnected clients. Remove subscription immediately on first send failure.

compounding_pairs.relationship: Even if WAL recovery is fixed (BUG-1), recovered entries STILL have wrong ordering because memtable sorts timestamps ascending (BUG-2). Both must be fixed for correct version semantics.
Two independent paths to the same symptom: deleted keys reappear. BUG-3 drops tombstones too early, BUG-4 misses boundary data. Agent must recognize these as SEPARATE bugs.
Even if replication catch-up is fixed (BUG-5), replicated data has wrong timestamps from the serialization mismatch (BUG-6). End-to-end verification requires fixing BOTH.
